name: RES4SHO logistic and Laplacian two-stage schedules
plain: Same two-stage layout as the atan family but with S-curves that have exponential tails: a logistic sigmoid (logistic, logistic_structure, logistic_detail) or a reversed Laplace CDF (laplacian). These bend more sharply near the pivot than arctangent, so the jump across the midpoint is larger for the same slope. logistic and laplacian use slope 0.20 in both stages; logistic_structure uses 0.10 then 0.30 and logistic_detail 0.30 then 0.10. Surprises shared by the whole family: a request for N steps returns N+1 steps (n = N+2 minus one junction value, plus a trailing 0); the split point is the linear midpoint of σ_max..σ_min with 60% of the steps above it, so on SD-style models (σ_max about 14.6) most steps sit above σ≈7.3; slopes are divided by n/40, so the shape changes with step count. Registered with use_ms=True; names already in the scheduler table are skipped, not overwritten.
math:
Symbols: N requested steps; σ_max, σ_min from the model; n = N + 2; m = int(0.6 n); σ_mid = σ_min + 0.5(σ_max − σ_min) (linear midpoint).
Stage 1: k = 0..m−1, pivot p1 = m, slope s1' = s1/max(n/40, 0.1); Stage 2: k = 0..n−m−1, pivot p2 = 0, slope s2' = s2/max(n/40, 0.1).
Each stage: r_k = curve(k; p, s'); r̂_k = (r_k − r_last)/(r_first − r_last); σ_k = end + r̂_k (start − end), stage 1 from σ_max to σ_mid, stage 2 from σ_mid to σ_min.
Output = stage 1 without its last value, stage 2, then 0: N+2 values, i.e. N+1 steps.
logistic: curve = 1/(1 + e^{s(k − p)}).
laplacian: u = s(k − p); curve = 1 − (½e^{u} if u ≤ 0 else 1 − ½e^{−u}).
Slopes (s1, s2): logistic (0.20, 0.20), logistic_structure (0.10, 0.30), logistic_detail (0.30, 0.10), laplacian (0.20, 0.20).

props.params: fixed by name; no inputs beyond steps
props.prints: draws an ASCII plot of the schedule to the console on every call
